item.title: France holds crisis talks after unrest
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
France holds crisis talks after unrest 2,400 detained amid riots as Macron rejects interior minister's resignation France's Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu convened an emergency cabinet session on Monday after more than 2,400 people were detained during two days of unrest across the country. Earlier in the day, President Emmanuel Macron rejected the resignation of Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, who had acknowledged that police had "lost control" of demonstrations, which first erupted last month over rising living costs and deteriorating conditions in schools but have now expanded. Nearly half a million people took to the streets on Saturday, according to authorities, with organizers claiming figures closer to 800,000. Some 110,000 marched in Paris alone. Most demonstrators gathered peacefully to protest, but the mood turned violent after masked, black-clad groups appeared among the crowds, the BBC reported. Around 1,500 businesses were ransacked and destroyed, and police responded with tear gas, water cannon and baton charges. The Interior Ministry said about 1,000 officers were injured, seven of them seriously. Vehicles were set ablaze across Paris and other cities in some of the worst disorder in years. In the central city of Limoges, flames destroyed the 19th-century town hall, in an apparent arson attack that caused its roof to collapse. Looting was reported in Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Rennes, Strasbourg and elsewhere. More than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters were injured. Addressing the nation on Sunday, Macron condemned the "shocking scenes" and those he called "dissenters" who had vandalized cities. "Those who looted will have to pay for the damage, and those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable," he said. Officials at the Elysee Palace said that Macron refused Nunez's resignation to ensure "continuous command of the law enforcement forces in the current context". Political opponents, trade unions and critics on social media have accused Nunez of failing to prepare adequately and deploying too few officers ahead of Saturday's planned demonstrations. Yael Braun-Pivet, president of the lower house of Parliament, has called for an inquiry into the security failures. Speculation had mounted that Macron might impose a curfew or declare a state of emergency to restore calm. Instead, the president used his televised address to appeal for national unity and promise that perpetrators would face justice. French media criticized the speech for lacking concrete measures. Prefects and mayors will be granted additional powers to ban gatherings, Macron announced, adding that a review would examine possible failings in intelligence or police preparedness. Sunday passed without major incident. Protests in Albania France was not the only country facing unrest over the weekend. In Albania, Prime Minister Edi Rama refused to resign after six days of violent anti-government protests in the capital Tirana. Demonstrators are demanding action over poor university conditions, high tuition fees and corruption. The unrest follows earlier protests against a resort development, linked to United States President Donald Trump, in a protected area. Police fired tear gas, water cannon and rubber bullets as crowds attacked a police station, the interior ministry, and Socialist Party headquarters with rocks and Molotov cocktails, Euronews reported. Authorities urged protesters to distance themselves from masked agitators and assemble peacefully. Police spokesman Albert Nushi said a Tirana police station came under attack, putting officers and those detained in custody at risk. "An attack on a police station is not a protest. Violence against police officers, attacks on institutions, and actions that endanger human lives cannot be tolerated," he said. Nushi called on demonstrators to avoid masked agitators and "assemble in a peaceful manner". jonathan@mail.chinadailyuk.com

item.title: China's therapies lead new cancer battle
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
China's innovative therapies lead new cancer battle 'Living drugs' entering overseas markets after Hong Kong success In July, a 59-year-old gastric cancer patient flew from New Zealand to Shanghai to have blood drawn for a world-leading China-developed treatment that targets solid tumors. Shanghai-based biopharmaceutical company CARsgen Therapeutics Holdings' satri-cel (satricabtagene autoleucel) treatment uses chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy. CAR-T therapy involves collecting T cells from a patient's blood and genetically modifying them before reinfusing them into the body so they can better recognize and attack cancer cells. The new procedure was given the all clear by the National Medical Products Administration in June — the world's first approved CAR T-cell therapy product for the treatment of solid tumors. Until satri-cel's arrival, commercial CAR T-cell products had been restricted to treating blood cancers. Conquering solid tumors, which make up most human cancers, marks a monumental leap for Chinese biotechnology, medical experts said. The breakthrough is mirrored by rapid commercial expansion of treatments, after the administration approved nine of the world's 17 commercial CAR T-cell products, seven of which were developed in China. China is neck-and-neck in a race with the United States for industry dominance. Of the top 10 institutions driving the world's 1,520 CAR T-cell research and development pipelines, half are from the Chinese mainland. Leading the pack is the Shenzhen Geno-Immune Medical Institute in Guangdong province, with 98 research and development pipelines. Fueled by a massive patient pool, rapid iteration as well as improved insurance and payout systems, China's CAR T-cell market is exploding and is forecast by one industry analysis to grow from $900 million last year to $16.18 billion by 2035. However, hurdles must be overcome for global expansion, including challenges such as the different classification of infectious materials in various jurisdictions and the transportation of "living drugs", industry figures said.

item.title: Measures set to stabilize finance market
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-20
Measures set to stabilize finance market Move to enhance liquidity support, facilitate cross-border investment China's top financial regulators pledged on Monday to strengthen financial market stability amid rising global volatility while advancing the sector's opening-up, unveiling a series of measures to enhance liquidity support and facilitate cross-border investment. Speaking at the opening of the Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum 2026 in Beijing, Wu Qing, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, said maintaining capital market stability remains a top priority, warning of growing spillover risks as volatility across global equity, bond and foreign exchange markets becomes increasingly interconnected. To strengthen market resilience, the CSRC will improve long-term performance assessment mechanisms for institutional investors, broaden channels for medium and long-term capital inflows and deepen mutual fund reforms. The regulator approved the registration of the country's first batch of 18 actively managed exchange-traded funds on Monday, a move Wu said will bring additional capital into the market. Listed companies will be encouraged to increase share buybacks and purchases by major shareholders, Wu said, while calling for heightened vigilance against leveraged products traded overseas that are linked to individual A-share stocks. Also at the opening, Pan Gongsheng, governor of the People's Bank of China, the country's central bank, announced plans to establish a liquidity backstop for large-scale redemptions by nonbank financial institutions, as a new macroprudential tool to stabilize the bond market. The facility would be activated under specific circumstances when asset managers face widespread liquidity stress and bond markets enter a negative feedback loop of redemptions and forced selling, while balancing systemic risk prevention against moral hazard. Eligible institutions will include bank wealth management subsidiaries, mutual fund managers and their parent banks or securities firms, Pan said. On financial opening-up, Pan said the PBOC will expand access to its standing lending facility — a monetary policy tool that provides collateralized financing to meet temporary liquidity needs — to cover all domestic deposit-taking financial institutions, including locally incorporated foreign banks. Pan said the central bank will roll out a pilot to allow overseas financial institutions to participate in renminbi trading in China's interbank foreign exchange market and extend access to its RMB repo facility — aimed at helping specific overseas institutions obtain yuan liquidity — to foreign-funded RMB clearing banks. Wu said the CSRC will facilitate investment under the Qualified Foreign Institutional Investor scheme, support domestic and international institutions in collaborating to launch more index products based on Chinese financial assets, and accelerate efforts to include RMB-denominated stock trading counters and real estate investment trusts in the Stock Connect programs. Ding Xiangqun, minister of the National Financial Regulatory Administration, pledged to deepen institutional opening-up, improve the regulatory environment for foreign institutions and encourage their participation in wealth management, pension and healthcare, and green finance. Zhu Hexin, head of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, said the regulator will introduce a package of capital account foreign exchange reforms to facilitate enterprises' cross-border investment and financing, while expanding a pilot program allowing securities firms to conduct foreign exchange settlement and sales. Zhang Linwan contributed to this story. zhoulanxv@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Improving demand fuels Q3 growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
Improving demand fuels Q3 growth China's stronger-than-expected 4.5 percent economic expansion in the third quarter, underpinned by new growth drivers and improving domestic demand, has boosted confidence that the world's second-largest economy will achieve its full-year growth target, officials and analysts said. The economy's strengthening momentum is expected to extend into the final quarter of the year, they said, as policymakers are directing greater efforts to further bolster domestic demand, with a particular focus on shoring up investment and restoring confidence in the property market. China's GDP growth accelerated to 4.5 percent year-on-year in the third quarter from 4.3 percent in the second, the National Bureau of Statistics said on Monday. Growth in the first three quarters stood at 4.6 percent, within the country's full-year target range of 4.5 to 5 percent. "We expect GDP growth to pick up further in the fourth quarter as growth-stabilizing policies take effect, leaving little doubt that China will achieve its full-year growth target," said Wang Qing, chief macroeconomic analyst at Orient Golden Credit Rating International. He attributed the pickup in third-quarter GDP growth mainly to faster industrial production, which expanded 5.1 percent year-on-year, up 0.4 percentage point from the second quarter. Advanced manufacturing, in particular, accounted for much of that strength. Equipment manufacturing output climbed 10.2 percent year-on-year in the first three quarters, while high-tech manufacturing grew 14.3 percent, the NBS said. Setting out priorities for the sector last month, President Xi Jinping emphasized the need to accelerate the development of a modernized industrial system with advanced manufacturing as the backbone, and to reinforce the foundations of the real economy, in an instruction conveyed at a national conference on advanced manufacturing held in Beijing. The latest figures point to a continued shift toward new growth drivers, said Mao Shengyong, deputy head of the NBS. "Preliminary estimates show that new growth drivers, led by advanced manufacturing, the digital and intelligent economy and modern services, contributed more than 40 percent of economic growth in the first three quarters," Mao said at a news conference in Beijing. Wang Jiaqiang, a senior researcher at the Bank of China Research Institute, said these sectors expanded at around 10 percent, describing their contribution to overall economic growth as "particularly significant". Domestic demand staged a modest rebound in September after softening in July and August. Retail sales — a key gauge of consumption — rose 1.1 percent year-on-year, up from 0.4 percent in August and the fastest pace since March, the NBS said. Meanwhile, fixed-asset investment showed signs of stabilizing, with the year-on-year decline holding at 7.2 percent in the first three quarters, halting a steady slowdown since March. Inflation has edged up alongside stronger domestic demand, with the GDP deflator — a broad measure of economy-wide prices — rising 1.5 percent year-on-year in the third quarter, its second straight quarter of positive growth, said Wang from Orient Golden Credit Rating International. Chen Mengyun, a macroeconomic analyst at Shenyin & Wanguo Futures, said, "The recovery in prices should help lift corporate earnings and strengthen nominal GDP growth." Still, analysts cautioned that the recovery in domestic demand remains tentative, underscoring the need for targeted policy support even as the full-year growth target looks well within reach. Further efforts to stabilize investment will be crucial, said Guo Liyan, deputy director of the Chinese Academy of Macroeconomic Research's Economic Research Institute. She called for closer policy coordination to make the most of the fourth-quarter construction window, with funding from new policy-based financial instruments reaching projects more quickly. Wang from Orient Golden Credit Rating expected stronger, coordinated fiscal and financial support for consumption. He also saw room for broader policy easing to sustain growth into next year. "There is still scope for growth-stabilizing measures, including across-the-board interest rate cuts, to help stabilize the economy," said Wang, who forecast that GDP growth would accelerate to around 4.7 percent in the fourth quarter. Global business leaders are similarly upbeat about China's prospects. Rogier Janssens, president of Merck China, said the company has invested nearly 7 billion yuan ($1.05 billion) in China, its second-largest market, over the past decade. "China's sustained push toward higher value-added manufacturing is modernizing the entire supply chain," he said.

item.title: Science seen as key to tackling global challenges
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
Science seen as key to tackling global challenges Science and technology are immensely important for addressing shared global challenges and achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, especially in a world where geopolitical tensions are rising, said experts at a global forum in Beijing on Monday. "Humanity's most pressing challenges — whether it's climate change, biodiversity loss, a pandemic, the health of our oceans and polar regions, or the regulation of technology for humanity's benefit — all demand worldwide cooperation," said Robbert Dijkgraaf, president-elect of the International Science Council, a nongovernmental international organization that provides scientific assessments and policy advice to the UN and global policymaking. "Without access to global data and expertise, we cannot understand these problems, let alone address them seriously," he said, noting that science is a global public good from which all people can benefit. Converging force Dijkgraaf stressed that science is one of the few converging forces in a fragmented world. "Scientists occupy what I might call the second ring of geopolitics — close enough to influence decisions, yet sufficiently independent to maintain relationships. When formal diplomacy becomes difficult, we might have less political power, but we have more freedom to act," he added. The remarks were made at the opening ceremony of the 2026 International Science Council Midterm Members' Meeting and Beijing Science Dialogue. Themed "Science in a Complex World, Science for a Better Future", the five-day event has attracted more than 1,200 delegates from over 80 countries and regions. Irina Bokova, former director-general of UNESCO, echoed Dijkgraaf's views, highlighting that scientific collaboration is "one of the conditions for making multilateralism work". "China is emerging as a strong supporter of the UN and multilateralism. China is promoting the equally important role science plays in the global governance agenda," she said, praising China's ambition to tackle core technologies and accelerate industrial application of results in basic research over the next five years. Brian Schmidt, a 2011 Nobel Laureate in Physics and former president of the Australian National University, mentioned that the astronomy link between Australian and Chinese scientists began in 1963, when there were no diplomatic ties between the two countries. "This act was permitted by both sides and ended up opening the door to Sino-Australian collaboration that has blossomed ever since," he said. "We should responsibly work together on science wherever we can. This cooperation might focus on global sustainability issues, but bottom-up work in any area of science also needs to be encouraged," he added. Pan Jianwei, a professor at the University of Science and Technology of China, said that "international academic exchange and cooperation are important drivers of scientific development", encouraging all parties to proactively integrate into the global innovation network and deepen international exchanges and cooperation in basic research. "China's economic strength and scientific research capabilities have risen significantly thanks to reform and opening-up over the past five decades. The country has both the responsibility and capacity to make its own important contributions to human scientific progress," he added.

item.title: In Nanjing, Autumn Arrives With the Scent of Osmanthus
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
For many locals in Nanjing, Jiangsu province, a date with the King Osmanthus is a cherished autumn ritual. Liu Guoyuan, 65, first visited the tree at the Zhongshan Mountain National Park more than 30 years ago, and he has come back almost every year. Most of the time he comes with his wife. "This area has such a pleasant environment and fresh air. Besides, the osmanthus blooms once a year — almost like a pact with autumn. If I miss it, I feel like autumn is incomplete," he said. The "King Osmanthus of Jinling" — Jinling was the name of Nanjing in ancient times — stands in a vast grassland north of the Linggu Temple. Spreading 12 to 14 meters across, the tree, which is more than 120 years old, has a wide canopy resembling a giant umbrella. When it is in blossom, dense flower clusters release a rich, intense fragrance. At peak bloom, the daily number of visitors surges, drawing local residents, photography enthusiasts and study-tour groups who come especially to admire the famous tree, according to Wang Chen, a senior landscape engineer at the attraction. Liu remembered that once, while resting under the King Osmanthus, gusts of wind showered the ground with osmanthus blooms and his child squatted down to pick up the petals. Chen Zhiyue, 24, traveled to Nanjing from Xi'an, Shaanxi province, especially to see the tree. "It is quite an awe-inspiring feeling standing beneath the tree," she said. "Its canopy is enormous, and countless tiny blossoms cluster thickly along every branch. Chen said that her work schedule is usually tight and stressful, and standing under the century-old tree lets her feel as if time has slowed to a gentle pace. "What touches me most about Nanjing's osmanthus is not how striking the blooms look, but how they are woven into everyday life," she said. Liu, the visitor, recalled that in the old days along the Qinhuai River, when autumn arrived, many people took painted pleasure boats for night cruises to breathe in the osmanthus fragrance. Street vendors sold osmanthus flower ornaments, which young girls wore in their hair. Some people would pick osmanthus blooms themselves to make osmanthus honey, taro dessert, cake and wine, a tradition passed down to modern days. Chen made an osmanthus sachet with the help of an instructor and bought osmanthus taro dessert at the Confucius Temple. "This is a flavor you can taste and a scent you can carry away," she added. For Nanjing residents, osmanthus is more than just an ornamental tree. It is a marker of the changing seasons. Autumn arrives in Nanjing not with red maple leaves, but with the first sweet whiff of osmanthus fragrance. More than 1 million osmanthus trees grow across Nanjing — lining roads and filling residential compounds and parks. According to Wang, the senior landscape engineer, the Linggu scenic area has grown osmanthus since 1261 and now has 18,000 trees of more than 20 varieties. There is also a naturally formed osmanthus corridor stretching about 300 meters. Elsewhere, the Yuhuatai scenic spot is home to another century-old osmanthus tree. The Xuanwu Lake boasts more than 2,000 osmanthus trees, and at the Mochou Lake, osmanthus trees dot the grounds beside pavilions and waterside terraces. In addition, the Zhanyuan Garden is home to two century-old golden osmanthus trees. Sun Qin, another senior landscape engineer at the Zhongshan Mountain National Park, said: "Osmanthus trees grow in ancient temples, imperial mausoleums and classical gardens, bearing the weight of history. They also thrive in residential compounds and along quiet city streets, woven into the daily lives of ordinary people."

item.title: Canada looks to China to diversify trade
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
Canada looks to China as trade diversification gains momentum Ottawa building economy less vulnerable to pressure from Washington, experts say Canada is stepping up efforts to diversify its trade as a renewed tariff confrontation with the United States puts fresh pressure on Ottawa to broaden its economic relationships. The US imposed a 50 percent tariff on C$27.6 billion ($19.6 billion) worth of Canadian goods effective Aug 22, prompting Canada to impose matching counter-tariffs on selected US products from Sept 8. The Canadian government has since emphasized the need to diversify trade and reduce dependence on any single partner. On Sept 29, a US ban on nearly $1 billion in annual imports from Canada took effect, targeting most Canadian alcoholic beverages, some dairy products and certain motorcycles. US President Donald Trump recently described Canada as "very difficult to deal with" and said: "Canada would like to make a deal, but we're not satisfied with it." Ron Stagg, a professor of history at Toronto Metropolitan University who studies Canadian-American relations, said the Canadian response to the latest US tariffs was being driven not only by economic considerations but also by growing frustration with what Ottawa sees as continuing demands from Washington. "Up until now the Carney government has treated the American government as a tough negotiator that will respond to conciliatory steps," Stagg told China Daily. "However, it is clear now that every time Canada gives a little, the US makes new demands," he said. He said the trade confrontation would reinforce Canada's efforts to build an economy that was less vulnerable to US pressure. China has emerged as one of the most significant destinations in that effort, with bilateral trade showing stronger export momentum in the first half of this year and both governments moving to restore market access in several areas. Canadian exports to China rose 30.1 percent year-on-year to C$21.74 billion in the first half of 2026, while imports from China fell 5.8 percent to C$44.86 billion, according to a report released by the Canada China Business Council and the China Institute at the University of Alberta. Total merchandise trade reached C$66.6 billion, up 3.6 percent from a year earlier. Bijan Ahmadi, executive director and COO of the Canada China Business Council, told China Daily the "most significant takeaway from the first half of 2026 is that Canada-China trade became more export-oriented". But the change in imports does not necessarily point to a broad retreat from Chinese products, he said. "The import decline was not a uniform retreat from Chinese supply: consumer goods and electronics weakened, while machinery, batteries and vehicles continued to grow," Ahmadi said, adding that full-year data would be needed before drawing broader conclusions. The report described the relationship as expanding "selectively rather than uniformly".

item.title: Young docents keep Long March story alive in Sichuan
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
Young docents keep Long March story alive in Sichuan In May 1935, Liu Bocheng, a Red Army commander, and Xiao Yedan, head of the Guoji clan of the Yi ethnic group, swore a blood oath by the Yihai Lake in Mianning county, Liangshan Yi autonomous prefecture, Sichuan province. The alliance enabled the Red Army to pass through Yi-inhabited areas and bought it time for the subsequent forced crossing of the Dadu River and the swift capture of the Luding Bridge during the Long March. More than 90 years later, young "Red Scarf" docents in Mianning are keeping the story alive. Moved by the story, one visitor said, "This must be told to more people." Since last year, more than 80 primary school students have taken part in docent training. While the storytellers change, ethnic unity and mutual support remain unchanged.

item.title: What stands out in China's sustainable development?
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-19
World Bank director Tatiana Rosito: In sustainable development, what stands out in China's experience? What stands out in China's experience of sustainable development? In a recent interview with China Daily's Global Lens, Tatiana Rosito, World Bank director for China, Mongolia and Korea, said China has "interesting, scalable and replicable" experience in its development, worth sharing with the world. She first affirms China's ecosystem restoration, adding that the Bank and China have worked together on fighting desertification and preventing erosion for more than 20 years. Then environmental solutions: China's experience in controlling air and water pollution is a ready-made example. And the rural-urban link — building sustainable, livable cities and a circular economy — is, she says, exactly the area developing partners most want to work on with China. Under the dual-carbon goals, the energy transition is likewise a good topic for knowledge cooperation. The "knowledge agenda" she describes runs both ways: inward, to help fill China's gaps; outward, using the World Bank's global reach and analytical skills to curate and translate Chinese solutions so other countries can adapt them to local conditions. In the next five years, she expects the World Bank to continue walking alongside China on sustainable development. (Reporter: Li Wei, Video: Pan Yixuan and Cheng Zixin)
